## GuacamayaSAR

An open Sentinel-1 SAR companion to Microsoft AI for Good's Project Guacamaya, built to
close the **cloud-cover gap** in optical Amazon deforestation monitoring. The Colombian
Amazon is cloud-covered for roughly half the year; during those months optical alerts go
quiet, and the operational SAR alert (Wageningen RADD) still misses real events.

Two complementary branches feed a fused change-detection model:

- **Amplitude branch** — OlmoEarth (AI2) as a frozen geospatial foundation backbone over
  Sentinel-1 RTC scenes from the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC catalog.
- **Coherence branch** — ASF HyP3 burst-InSAR pairs producing interferometric coherence
  and unwrapped phase, wired into a `torch.complex64` tensor. This phase-preserving,
  complex-valued head is the novel contribution: coherence collapses on disturbance
  independent of brightness.

Headline metric: **recall on a curated set of 66 RADD-missed deforestation events** over
Florencia, Caquetá.

[Repository →](https://github.com/josiahwsmith10/GuacamayaSAR){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}

## NISAR L-band geo-FM gap

Every public geospatial foundation model was pretrained on **C-band** SAR. NISAR is
**L-band** — it penetrates vegetation canopy and has fundamentally different scattering
physics. The wedge: frozen C-band-pretrained FMs should *not* transfer zero-shot to
L-band NISAR. This project quantifies the gap by class, then proposes a phase-aware,
truly complex-valued adapter on a frozen FM — leaning into L-band's real advantage for
biomass under canopy.

NISAR began continuous global L-band collection in Aug 2025, with calibrated products
arriving mid-2026 — a narrow window in which "first published geo-FM evaluation on NISAR"
is still unclaimed.

*Write-up in progress — see the [Blog](blog.qmd).*

## ideas-geospatial

A working notebook of geospatial research ideas being scoped and pruned, including the
NISAR L-band FM gap above, cross-sensor super-resolution, and an open ComSAR agent.
